proposed.text: A concrete masonry unit (CMU) partition wall must achieve a 2-hour fire resistance rating. Comparing the required partition thickness to the 1-hour requirement, which statement correctly describes the code relationship?

options.text: The 2-hour wall requires exactly double the thickness of the 1-hour wall, which is a common misconception as fire resistance does not scale linearly
The 2-hour wall requires a proportionally larger thickness increase than the step from 2-hour to 3-hour, due to the nonlinear behavior of materials under fire conditions
The partition thickness scales linearly with fire rating from 1-hour through 4-hour, which is not accurate as material properties affect the scaling
The thickness increments between adjacent fire ratings are not constant because material behavior is nonlinear

proposed.rationale: Original question was already source-correct and substantive; the prior edit (source-audited-article-batch-048) was degenerate, with 1-character garbage in 3 of 4 option text fields and a nonsensical rationale. Restored the original verbatim. Original source rationale: Sec. 603 partition thickness requirements reflect the nonlinear relationship between wall mass and fire resistance duration. Each rating step does not produce a proportional thickness increase because heat transfer through masonry is a time-dependent, nonlinear process.
proposed.explanation: Fire resistance testing of masonry walls shows diminishing returns at higher ratings — a wall twice as thick does not provide twice the fire resistance. The code tables reflect tested values, not calculated proportions. This explains why RC slab thicknesses plateau (both 3-hour and 4-hour require 150mm) while cover requirements continue to increase.
